cards.design_implication: If modeling transient emissions in design-only research, one may adopt a framework where luminosity is powered by r-process decay of ejecta, but must verify this against specific spectral signatures rather than assuming it as a default for all short gamma-ray burst afterglows.
does_not_establish: Empirical proof that this mechanism operated in a specific unobserved event without spectral confirmation.
Quantitative parameters for the decay rate or ejecta mass required for this mechanism to produce observable emission.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Neutron star binary mergers are also expected, however, to produce isotropic electromagnetic signals, which include (i) early optical and infrared emission, a so-called kilonova/macronova (hereafter kilonova; Li & Paczyński 1998; Kulkarni 2005; Rosswog 2005; Metzger et al. 2010; Roberts et al. 2011; Barnes & Kasen 2013; Kasen et al. 2013; Tanaka & Hotokezaka 2013; Grossman et al. 2014; Barnes et al. 2016; Tanaka 2016; Metzger 2017) due to radioactive decay of rapid neutron-capture process (r-process) nuclei (Lattimer & Schramm 1974, 1976) synthesized in dynamical and accretion-disk-wind ejecta during the merger;
limitations: The statement refers to what is 'expected' based on theoretical models.
It describes a general mechanism applicable to neutron star mergers, not necessarily all compact object mergers.
cards.statement: The text describes a theoretical mechanism for kilonovae/macronovae, positing that they arise from isotropic electromagnetic signals driven by the radioactive decay of r-process nuclei synthesized in merger ejecta.

cards.design_implication: When designing multi-messenger observation plans, one should treat early UV/optical/IR data and late X-ray/radio data as potentially originating from different physical components (e.g., kilonova vs. afterglow), requiring separate analytical models or causal isolation.
does_not_establish: The identity of the physical process generating the X-ray/radio emission (e.g., relativistic jet).
The exact causal mechanism for the UV/optical/IR emission in this sentence.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Both the X-ray and radio emission likely arise from a physical process that is distinct from the one that generates the UV/optical/near-infrared emission.
limitations: The text uses the qualifier 'likely', indicating this is an inference rather than a definitively established fact in this specific context.
The specific nature of the 'distinct' process is not defined in this excerpt.
cards.statement: X-ray and radio emissions discovered days after the optical transient are attributed to a physical process distinct from the UV/optical/near-infrared emission mechanism.

cards.design_implication: In designs relying solely on gravitational-wave waveform fitting for source classification, one must acknowledge a boundary where EM follow-up or other messengers are required to distinguish neutron stars from black holes or exotic compact objects, even when mass parameters appear compatible.
does_not_establish: A universal rule that GW data can never distinguish neutron stars from black holes.
The specific physical properties of quark stars or black holes that would remain indistinguishable in GW data for other events.
cards.evidence_excerpt: However, for this event gravitational-wave data alone cannot rule out objects more compact than neutron stars such as quark stars or black holes (Abbott et al. 2017c).
limitations: This limitation is explicitly noted for 'this event' (GW170817) and may depend on signal-to-noise ratio and detector bandwidth.
It does not preclude ruling out objects based on combined GW and EM data.
cards.statement: Gravitational-wave data alone for the analyzed binary neutron star candidate cannot rule out objects more compact than neutron stars, such as black holes or quark stars, despite component masses consistent with neutron stars.
